seo.title: Nuaj Studio — Handmade Textile Art & Custom Commissions
seo.description: Nuaj Studio is the textile art practice of Stephanie Onuaja: mixed-media pieces cut, composed and stitched by hand from lace, aso-oke and beads. Custom textile art commissions for homes, hotels, offices and public spaces.
seo.ogImageAlt: Close-up of cobalt lace strips with mint leaf appliqués stitched over gold aso-oke — Nuaj Studio

hero.intro: I cut, compose and stitch lace, aso-oke and beads into textile art — made by hand, for the spaces and people it belongs to.

reveal.caption: Every Nuaj piece is made by hand, in three movements.

manifesto.label: The studio
manifesto.statement: I take lace, aso-oke and beads — cloth that already carries meaning — and *cut, compose and stitch* them into pieces made for one place, and for the people who live with it.
manifesto.aside: Nuaj is the textile practice of Stephanie Onuaja. Every piece starts by hand, at the cutting table, and is finished by hand — one strip, one bead, one stitch at a time.
manifesto.question: Where does a story begin?

items.title: Textile design
items.text: Original surfaces built from lace, aso-oke and beads — cut into strips, layered and stitched into new cloth.
items.alt: Cobalt lace scattered with sequins and silver thread

items.title: Wearables
items.text: I design and sew clothing in colour and pattern reminiscent of my origins — garments made from my own textiles.
items.alt: Collage from Stephanie's sketchbook: a dress she designed and sewed from African-print fabrics, with handwritten notes
items.note: fashion is self-expression — it is who I am

items.title: Commissions
items.text: Wall pieces and installations for homes, hotels, offices and public spaces — designed around your story and your room.
items.alt: Finished mosaic of cobalt lace strips over gold aso-oke

process.label: Process
title: From cloth
to story

steps.title: Gather
steps.text: It starts with fabric that means something — lace, aso-oke, beads, sometimes cloth you bring me.
steps.alt: Mint and gold guipure lace, one of the fabrics gathered for the piece

steps.title: Cut
steps.text: I cut the cloth into strips and shapes by hand, following the pattern already in the lace.
steps.alt: Cobalt lace cut into wavy strips, laid out on the table

steps.title: Compose
steps.text: The pieces are laid out, moved and layered until the composition holds together.
steps.alt: Hands arranging cut lace strips and leaves on aso-oke

steps.title: Stitch
steps.text: Everything is stitched and beaded into place — one finished piece, made to last.
steps.alt: Close-up of lace strips and leaves being stitched onto gold aso-oke

process.question: How can we shape materials into artifacts?

commission.text: Custom textile art for your home, hotel, office or public space — made from your idea, and sometimes from your own fabric.

steps.title: Tell me your idea
steps.text: Share what you have in mind and any fabrics you'd like to use.

steps.title: I send a quote
steps.text: You'll get a design idea, a price, and a timeline.

steps.title: I make your piece
